_comment: Sources tracked by COMMIT, not by PyPI release. See deps/README.md for why.
This file is the single source of truth for all three. Nothing here belongs
in pyproject.toml: a direct-reference (git+) dependency makes the whole
distribution un-publishable to PyPI, and these move far faster than their
PyPI registrations. Fetch them with `python deps/fetch.py`.
Bump `commit` deliberately, never automatically. Record why in `pinned_because`.

cobrakbase.pypi: cobrakbase 0.3.0 (2022-12) — over three years behind the repo
pinned_because: Fxe/cobrakbase@master is what ModelSEED/modelseed-api installs, so it is
what backs modelseed.org. cshenry/cobrakbase is a fork 141 commits behind
Fxe and is used only by KB-ModelSEEDReconstruction; do not use it.
Note Fxe's DEFAULT branch is `cobra-model`, not `master` — modelseed-api
explicitly selects master, so we match that rather than the default.
ADAPTER-ONLY. cobrakbase/__init__.py unconditionally constructs KBaseAPI
and vendors a 364 KB workspace client, so it must never be imported by
the science core. Enforced by Core/tests/test_core_isolation.py.

modelseedpy.pypi: ModelSEEDpy 0.4.2 (2025-03) — lags the fork by well over a year
pinned_because: cshenry/ModelSEEDpy is the de-facto build: modelseed-api clones it
(--branch main) and so does KB-ModelSEEDReconstruction. It is ~117
commits ahead of ModelSEED/ModelSEEDpy@dev and carries MSFBA,
msminimalmedia and a much larger msexpression.
install is no-deps ON PURPOSE: the fork pins scikit-learn==1.2.0, which
cannot build on Python 3.12 (needs distutils, removed in 3.12). Only
modelseedpy/ml and helpers.get_classifier need sklearn and we use
neither. modelseed-api works around the same pin by force-reinstalling
numpy+scikit-learn afterwards; KB-ModelSEEDReconstruction uses pip's
legacy resolver.
Usage constraints: always pass annotate_with_rast=False (the True
default makes an outbound ANL call — breaks reproducibility and CTS's
no-runtime-downloads rule), and never call helpers.get_template or
helpers.get_classifier at runtime (they write into site-packages).
This is the ModelSEED biochemistry DATABASE — not ModelSEEDpy. Both are
needed and they are different things.
The commit is the one already chosen in Generate_Core_ModelTemplate.py
(MSD_PINNED_COMMIT): immediately BEFORE 6a3813875f, the 2026-05-29
reversibility refresh, so reaction directions match what the published
templates were generated against. That script is the reason this pin
exists; this file is now where it lives.
LAYOUT WARNING — dev and master are structurally different branches.
dev (this pin, and its tip) stores biochemistry as 111 sharded JSON
files, Biochemistry/reaction_NN.json and compound_NN.json, and has no
Templates/ directory and no reactions.tsv or compounds.tsv at all.
master has the classic single reactions.tsv + compounds.tsv plus
Templates/. PlantSEED reads the sharded dev form — see the
reaction_.*\.json / compound_.*\.json patterns in
Generate_Core_ModelTemplate.py — so dev is correct for us. But
ModelSEEDpy's own biochem loader expects master's TSVs, so anything
going through modelseedpy will need the master layout instead. Do not
assume one checkout serves both.
SIZE, measured not estimated: the full repo is 1.32 GB; these two
patterns yield 111 files / 189 MB (reaction_*.json 142 MB over 61
files, compound_*.json 48 MB over 50), plus ~18 MB of .git. That is
considerably more than master's TSV form and it matters for container
size — consider a build-time conversion to a compact cache (PlantSEED
already pickles these into Biochem_Cache/MS_Rxns.pickle and
MS_Cpds.pickle) rather than shipping the JSON.
Sparse checkout is --no-cone: cone mode understands directory prefixes
only and silently ignores file-level patterns, pulling whole
directories instead (394 MB, and still missing the files we asked for).
modelseed-api tracks the moving dev tip rather than pinning, so
modelseed.org and our templates can disagree on reaction directionality.
